title: Merge sort and inversions
description:
```cpp
template <class T, class Less = std::less<T>> void mergeSort(std::vector<T>& a, Less less = Less{});   // stable, O(n log n)
long long countInversions(std::vector<int> a);                                                       // O(n log n)
std::vector<int> mergeAll(const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& lists);                               // merge sorted lists pairwise
```

- `mergeSort` must be stable and allocate its buffer **once**, not in every call.
- `countInversions` counts pairs `i < j` with `a[i] > a[j]` while merge sorting (lesson 3.02). The tests use 100,000 elements, which have up to 5 × 10⁹ inversions, so count with `long long` and do not compare every pair.
- `mergeAll` merges any number of sorted lists by merging them **in pairs, round after round** (like the levels of merge sort): with k lists of n elements in total, that is O(n log k). No `std::sort` allowed here.
hints: When the merge takes `a[j]` from the right half, every element still waiting in the left half, `a[i..mid)`, is bigger: add `mid - i` inversions.
To merge in rounds: merge lists 0 and 1, 2 and 3, and so on into a new vector of lists (carrying an odd one over), and repeat until one list is left.
